summary: Somerset County, ME tower on Number 5 Mountain in TNC's Leuthold Forest Preserve; built 1933 per Press Herald; listed standing; TNC warns people not to climb it.

facts.agency: The Nature Conservancy (owns and manages the Leuthold Forest Preserve)

access.note: The preserve trail is open, but The Nature Conservancy has removed the tower's lower steps and warns people not to climb it

visit.trail_note: The old fire warden's trail from the south is about six miles round trip to the summit ledges and tower; TNC warns people not to climb the tower

events.note: Press Herald (2019): 'erected in 1933'; the builder is not named in the sources read
As of the June 2019 Press Herald column, TNC had removed the tower's lower steps and restored the trail; the year the steps came off is not given

notes_for_editor: Read: Press Herald 2019 (built 1933; lower steps removed; trail restored; 6-mile round trip), Maine by Foot (intact tower; TNC warns people not to climb), FFLA Maine standing list (no asterisk, so cab not marked missing). Not found: builder, tower height or design, staffing history, current condition, any visiting rules beyond TNC's warning. Elevation disagrees: 3,186 ft (Press Herald) vs 3,183 ft (Maine by Foot); not used in the story. A Facebook post dated Nov 3, 2025, seen only as a search snippet and not fetched, says the tower still stands with only a partial cab; not used, but worth checking against the FFLA listing. The Maine State Archives 'No. 5 Mt.' panorama map is for T6 R7 WELS, Penobscot County, a different mountain. Used 2 WebSearch and about 6 page reads.
